title: Best-of-n, weighted voting, and PRM-guided beam search
brief: Compute best-of-n's expected reward exactly, build majority and weighted voting, then steer beam search on a toy with a known step-level value.
hints: For best_of_n_expected_reward, sort the outcomes by reward and take F = np.cumsum of their probabilities. The chance that the max is outcome i is F_i**n - F_{i-1}**n, with F_0 = 0.

For the votes, np.eye(n_answers)[answers] turns (B, n) answers into (B, n, n_answers) one-hots. Multiply by the weights and sum over the samples axis, then np.argmax, which returns the first maximum, so ties go to the smallest answer.

step_values runs backward from values[T] = one-hot of the target. values[t, s] = sum over digits a of step_probs[t, a] * values[t + 1, s + a]. Pad values[t + 1] with V zeros so s + a past the end reads zero.
In prm_beam_search, build candidates with np.repeat(beams, n_tokens, axis=0) and np.tile(np.arange(n_tokens), len(beams)). np.argsort(-scores, kind='stable') keeps ties in candidate order.
